# Site package basics

This part of the site packages help explains how a package is built and how Exponential reads it. It is for
administrators who install sites and want to know what happens, and for developers who change or write packages.
Every statement on these pages was checked against the kernel code of 6.0.15 (`kernel/classes/ezpackage.php` and
the classes around it), `settings/package.ini`, the package sources and the live package server.

If you only want to install a site, you do not need any of this: the setup wizard, the kickstarter and
`exp:install` do it for you (see [Choosing an install method](../../../install/04-choosing-an-install-method.md)).
Read on when an install fails, when you want to change what a new site contains, or when you build a package.

## The basics in ten lines

1. A **package** is a directory with a definition file (`package.xml`, or `package.json` in the JSON format) and the
   files it names.
2. Shipped as one file, a package is a gzip compressed tar archive ending in `.ezpkg`.
3. Every package has a **type** (`<type value="..."/>`); a **site package** has the type `site`.
4. A site package **requires** other packages (`<require type="ezpackage" name="..." min-version="..."/>`): content
   classes, content, extensions, site styles.
5. A site package can carry **install scripts** (`<settings><settings-file filename="..."/>`) that set up
   siteaccesses, settings, roles and preferences.
6. The packages it requires carry **install items** (`<install><item type="..."/>`), each handled by a
   **package handler** named in `settings/package.ini [PackageSettings] HandlerAlias[]`.
7. **Import** puts a package into the local repository, `var/storage/packages/<vendor>/<name>/`; nothing on the site
   changes.
8. **Install** runs the install items. Packages with `install_type="import"` (every site package of the 6.0.15
   index) have nothing to install themselves.
9. The setup wizard, the kickstarter and `exp:install` all run the same steps from
   `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_data.php`: they find the site package, import it and its requirements, install the
   requirements, and call the install scripts.
10. Packages come from the **package server**, whose address is `settings/package.ini [RepositorySettings]
    RemotePackagesIndexURL`; see [The package server](../package-server/README.md).

## Where the code is

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| The package model: read, write, import, install, uninstall | `kernel/classes/ezpackage.php` (`eZPackage`) |
| Archive checks before anything is written | `kernel/classes/ezpackageuploadinspector.php` |
| Version comparison (`min-version`) | `kernel/classes/ezpackageversion.php` |
| Install item handlers | `kernel/classes/packagehandlers/*/` |
| Package creation wizards | `kernel/classes/packagecreators/*/` |
| Step installers of the administration | `kernel/classes/packageinstallers/*/` |
| The administration's package views | `kernel/package/` (entry points), `kernel/private/classes/views/package/` |
| The setup steps that use packages | `kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php`, `ezstep_package_language_options.php`, `ezstep_create_sites.php` |
| The command line package manager | `ezpm.php` in the installation root, code in `kernel/private/classes/commands/ezpm.php` |
| Settings | `settings/package.ini` |
